question: How do I start a men's group?
seo_title: How to Start a Men's Group at Church or Online | TheWrkShop
description: Start small: three to eight men, one regular time, a simple rhythm and one rule of honesty. A practical, biblical guide with free printable tools.
answer: Start small and start honest: invite three to eight men you'd trust with the truth, pick one regular time, and use a simple rhythm of Scripture, honest questions and prayer. A men's group doesn't need a big program. It needs a room where men stop performing and start being known.

sections.heading: Why most men's groups fade
paragraphs: Most groups don't fail because of bad content. They fail because nobody tells the truth. Men show up, talk about sports and opinions, nod through a study, and go home carrying exactly what they brought.

What a community punishes, men learn to hide. If a confession gets a joke, or a struggling marriage gets awkward silence, the room has just taught everyone what not to say. So the first job of a group leader isn't teaching. It's making honesty safe.

sections.heading: A simple way to begin
list: **Who:** three to eight men. Small enough that nobody can hide.
**When:** the same time every week or every other week. Consistency matters more than length.
**Where:** a living room, a coffee shop corner or a video call. Online works.
**How long:** 60–75 minutes. End on time so men keep coming.
**One rule:** what's said here stays here, and nobody fixes anyone without being asked.

sections.heading: A rhythm that works
paragraphs: Open with one honest check-in question ("Where are you really this week?"). Read one short passage. Ask two or three questions that go beneath behavior to what's driving it. Pair men up to pray for each other during the week. Close with one step each man will take before you meet again.
The [Men's Group Starter Kit](/sub-pages/resources/starter-kit.html) has a first-four-weeks plan, a meeting agenda, a group covenant and a facilitator one-pager you can print for free.

scriptures.text: Though one may be overpowered, two can defend themselves. A cord of three strands is not quickly broken.
And let us consider how we may spur one another on toward love and good deeds, not giving up meeting together….
Therefore confess your sins to each other and pray for each other so that you may be healed.

steps: Write down five men you'd trust with the truth. Text three of them today.
Pick a day, time and place for four weeks. Ask for a four-week commitment, not forever.
Print the free [group covenant and meeting agenda](/sub-pages/resources/starter-kit.html).
At the first meeting, go first. Share one honest thing. The room follows the leader's honesty.

faqs.q: Do I need to be a pastor or Bible teacher to lead a men's group?
faqs.a: No. You need to be honest, consistent and willing to go first. A simple guide like the [Starter Kit](/sub-pages/resources/starter-kit.html) carries the structure so you can focus on the men.

faqs.q: How many men should be in a men's group?
faqs.a: Three to eight. Fewer than three loses energy; more than eight lets men hide. When a group grows past eight, split it.

faqs.q: Can a men's group meet online?
faqs.a: Yes. Video groups work well, especially for men with travel or shift schedules. Keep cameras on and the group small. TheWrkShop's own groups meet online; [get known](/get-known.html) to join one.
